props.gloss_en: the first tanna: R' Elazar ben Azarya says the musaf prayer is only [recited] in a chever ir
the Sages: [the musaf prayer is recited] with a chever ir and without a chever ir
R' Yehuda in his name: wherever there is a chever ir, the individual is exempt from the musaf prayer
R' Yehuda's position is the same as the first tanna's
the difference between them is an individual who is not in a chever ir
the first tanna holds [the individual not in a chever ir] exempt
and R' Yehuda holds [the individual not in a chever ir] obligated
the halakha is as R' Yehuda, who said it in R' Elazar ben Azarya's name
Shmuel: in all my days I never prayed the musaf prayer as an individual in Nehardea
except the day the king's army came to the city and the Rabbis were troubled and did not pray, and I prayed as an individual, and I was an individual not in a chever ir
R' Yannai: the halakha is not as R' Yehuda, who said it in R' Elazar ben Azarya's name
R' Yochanan: I saw R' Yannai pray and then pray again

supports.gloss_en: שפיר קאמרת, דאמר שמואל: מימי לא מצלינא צלותא דמוספין ביחיד בנהרדעא -- Shmuel never prayed musaf alone where there was a chever ir
...except the day of the king's army, when he prayed alone, והואי יחיד שלא בחבר עיר -- the one time he prayed alone, he was an individual not in a chever ir
אני ראיתי את רבי ינאי דצלי והדר צלי -- R' Yochanan saw R' Yannai pray and pray again (Steinsaltz: the second prayer was musaf, so R' Yannai acted against R' Yehuda's view; the text does not say so)
